idiom_name: list.append through a passed list (io.StringIO for text)
implementation_notes: Pass a list and let producers call `list.append`/`extend`; it is the direct translation of Beck's Smalltalk pattern and needs no framework support, since arguments are references to the same object. The Pythonic alternative is usually better for whole collections - build and return a value with a list comprehension or generator expression - and for text the documentation recommends building a list and calling `str.join()`, or writing to an `io.StringIO`, rather than repeated concatenation. Keep the accumulator form when the result is produced by a call tree (recursive walk, several collaborating methods) rather than one comprehensible loop.
pitfalls: Never use a mutable default (`def collect(out=[])`): the same list is reused across calls and every result accumulates forever.
Lists are shared, not copied: a callee that sorts, clears or rebinds (`out = out + [x]`) the accumulator either changes the caller's object or silently stops contributing.
Threads and async tasks appending to one list interleave nondeterministically; use queues or per-task lists plus a merge.
